extracted.subtask_description: A wire-service newspaper article reporting multiple Cold War–era diplomatic, military, and political events (e.g., U.S.-Japan transfers, congressional hearings, Bandung Conference speeches). Intended as factual reporting for a broad readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Geneva agreements on Indochina (implementation requirements)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Geneva agreements provide that Indochinese states shall not join any military alliance and that no foreign military bases should be established in these states. They are to be respected to restore peace in Indochina on the basis of respect for the right to national independence and with support of the conference of five Colombo powers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why the Geneva conference was able to create favorable conditions for peace; states that the Geneva agreements "should be strictly and faithfully carried out with no interference or obstruction from any quarter."

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for independence, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Any settlement (e.g., on Indochina, Korea) should be based on respect for the independence, sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of the states concerned and not to interfere in their internal affairs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as a necessary basis for peace and for allowing peoples to choose their own political systems without outside interference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five principles of peaceful coexistence (guiding mutual-relations principles)
rubrics_metrics.description: China and Burma have affirmed five principles of peaceful coexistence as guiding principles in their mutual relations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece links these principles to promotion of mutual understanding and cooperation; while the article does not list each principle verbatim, it situates them as foundational to normalizing relations and avoiding use of conferences to publicize ideology or create divergence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-interference as prerequisite for self-determination
rubrics_metrics.description: "If nations give us an assurance not to interfere in each other's internal affairs, it will then be possible for the people of those countries to choose their own political system and way of life."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a condition for genuine national independence and peaceful development; tied to implementing Geneva accords and peaceful unification of Korea.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction and prohibition of armaments and atomic weapons
rubrics_metrics.description: Asian and African countries (per Chou) demand that big powers should reach agreement on reduction of armaments and "prohibition of atomic weapons and all other weapons of mass destruction," and that atomic energy be used for peaceful purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Posited as a popular demand of peoples opposed to preparations for war; presented as a concrete policy objective for preserving world peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Economic cooperation: equality, mutual benefit, and independent development
rubrics_metrics.description: Economic cooperation should be based on equality and mutual benefit with no conditions for privilege attached; trade relations and economic cooperation should promote independent economic development in each country and not convert any country into a sole producer of raw materials and market for consumer goods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Framed as necessary to eliminate backwardness caused by colonial exploitation and to ensure development rather than dependence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural exchange with respect for national culture
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural exchange should have respect for development of national culture of each country and not ignore characteristics and special merits of culture of any country so that we may learn and benefit from each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presented as a component of closer Asian-African cooperation and mutual understanding; warns against cultural domination or erasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal rights in international relations and fundamental human rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Countries, whether big or small, strong or weak, should all enjoy equal rights in international relations; their territorial integrity and sovereignty should not be violated; people, irrespective of race or color, should all enjoy fundamental human rights and not be subjected to maltreatment and discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raised as a political and moral demand tied to the end of colonialism and to the legitimacy of newly independent states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strict and faithful carrying out of international agreements (no obstruction)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Geneva agreements on the restoration of peace in Indochina should be strictly and faithfully carried out with no interference or obstruction from any quarter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes implementation fidelity as essential to preserving the favorable conditions for peace created by the Geneva Conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peaceful unification principle (Korea) — apply same standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The question of peaceful unification of Korea should be solved in accordance with the same principles (non-interference, respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity) applied to Indochina and other disputes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as an extension of the Geneva-based principles to other regional unification issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness rights under the Fifth Amendment (procedural protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: A witness may refuse to answer questions on the grounds of the Fifth Amendment; the Fifth Amendment "guarantees that no man can..." be compelled to incriminate himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contextualized in congressional/FCC hearings where witnesses invoke the Fifth to decline answering questions about alleged associations; presented as a standard legal protection in U.S. procedure.
